text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: high GPU queue growth in east1-primary. 90th-p99 latency spike and elevated 429s since 02:03 UTC. Autoscaler failing to acquire capacity (quota errors). Paging oncall.

alex: saw this spike in the dashboard. queue depth at the serving layer jumped from ~300 -> 2.4k over 4min. tokens/sec dropped, requests enqueued.

priya: paging mike oncall now. any recent deploys to east1? /cc @mike_oncall

mike_oncall: on it. grabbing logs. starting investigation. can someone post the autoscaler error snippet?

jamie: past 5m from autoscaler:
```
ERROR autoscaler: unable to provision GPU nodes: quotaExceeded: Requested 16 gpus, but quota allows 8
caller=autoscaler/driver.go:182
```
Also seeing API rate limit errors to cloud provider: 429 on node-create calls.

mike_oncall: ah — so autoscaler hit quota *and* provider API throttling. that explains partial failures. routing still believes east1 has capacity and isn't spilling over.

alex: routing policy for east1 is "prefer-primary" with conservative spillover. it only fails over when instance count==0. we probably need to relax that to avoid long queues when autoscaler is backing off.

priya: customer impact: a subset of production traffic to Redwood API (hosted) is seeing >10s tails and some 429s. SLO alerts triggered. No total outage yet. large customers reported degraded latency.

sre-bot: Incident severity: sev2. Notify product + support. Incident channel: #incidents. Runbook: gpu-capacity-exhaustion.

mike_oncall: mitigation plan (short):
1) enable immediate spillover to west1 for non-data-resident requests
2) temporarily reduce concurrency limit for low-priority tenants (throttle) to shed load
3) attempt manual provisioning via cloud console for 8 GPUs as emergency burst (if quota permits)
4) update routing policy to allow speculative failover at queue depth > 500

jamie: toggled traffic tag for non-prod and low-priority customers to route-west1: `POST /routing/config` payload applied.

alex: command we ran to lower tenant concurrency for bursty accounts:
```
PATCH /tenants/config
{ "priority_groups": { "low": { "concurrency_limit": 2 } } }
```
Applied. should reduce new enqueue rate from low-tier clients.

mike_oncall: started manual node create in console — but provider reports API rate-limited. opening support ticket with provider. ETA unknown.

priya: support notified top-3 impacted customers via status page and direct outreach. messaging: "degraded latency in east1, mitigation in progress, fallback routing to west1 enabled for eligible traffic."

jamie: routing change metrics: west1 inflight increased ~18% in last 2m. queue in east1 growth has slowed but still high; tokens/sec recovering slightly.

mike_oncall: quick check of sticky routing config — noticed route affinity TTL is 15m; that prevents some sessions from being moved to west1 even though we enabled spillover. lowering TTL to 30s for the emergency.

alex: changed affinity TTL: `routing/affinity:set --ttl 30s --scope emergency` — applied. that should let in-flight sessions migrate on reconnect.

sre-bot: note: reducing affinity can impact session consistency for customers relying on local cache. create mitigation note for post-incident.

mike_oncall: manual provisioning attempt succeeded for 4 GPUs (partial). cloud still throttling further requests but we have some relief. queue drops ~22% after the first nodes came online.

priya: product wants to know whether to enable broader spillover (all traffic) or keep limited. thoughts?

alex: recommend keep limited to non-data-resident and stateless endpoints. broad failover might expose latency variability and cross-region data egress costs.

jamie: agree. also we should escalate quota increase with provider; open a ticket with subject "urgent quota bump — east1 GPUs — Redwood Inference" and request temporary raise to 64 GPUs.

mike_oncall: created ticket #{"PR-4621"} with provider support and included recent autoscaler errors and impact. provider acknowledged rate limiting, investigating.

sre-bot: timeline checkpoint: 02:03 UTC alert -> 02:06 enable spillover -> 02:10 affinity TTL reduced -> 02:13 first manual nodes up -> 02:17 queue trending down. moving to mitigation phase.

priya: handing off to next oncall (jamie) in 30m for monitoring and follow-up. we'll keep this channel for updates. please add any customer notes.

jamie: taking over monitoring. will watch queue for 1hr and hold on additional routing changes unless we see re-spike. leaving note in incident tracker.

alex: follow-ups for postmortem:
- make autoscaler aware of provider API throttling and implement exponential-backoff+retry jitter
- change routing policy thresholds for speculative spillover based on queue depth, not absolute capacity
- run quota reviews per-region and automate quota increase requests when usage trends exceed threshold
- add runbook step for affinity TTL emergency change and consequences

priya: support to update affected customers: status page updated and emails sent. request for timeline draft for customer success.

mike_oncall: resolving pager for now — root cause: concurrent provider-side quota + API throttling prevented autoscaler from provisioning capacity quickly, causing queue growth; mitigation: spillover + manual provisioning + throttling low-priority clients.

sre-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. please create postmortem ticket and assign owners (autoscaler work: alex, routing thresholds: jamie, quota automation: priya).

jamie: ack. adding owners and ETA for follow-ups in task tracker.

priya: I'll draft the initial postmortem and customer-facing summary this afternoon.

mike_oncall: thanks all. handing off final monitoring to jamie. if we see another spike, re-open page.

sre-bot: :white_check_mark: Thread closed for now. Remember to link logs + metrics to postmortem ticket."
